+# Artifact SDK compatibility
+
+This action keeps the official `@actions/artifact` client for authentication,
+immutable artifact IDs, digests and transport. Scoped npm overrides pin the
+SDK's original `unzip-stream` 0.3.4 and replace `archiver-utils`' deprecated
+glob 10.5.0 with glob 14.0.3, which preserves the only API it uses,
+`glob.sync`.
+
+Downloads use the SDK's documented `skipDecompress` option and pass the digest
+recorded at upload time as `expectedHash`, so the SDK still verifies every
+downloaded archive. `zip.js` 2.24.0 then extracts it. The SDK's own reader,
+unzip-stream, constructs deprecated `Buffer` instances; zip.js has no runtime
+dependencies and supports ZIP64 and streamed decompression.
+
+## Adapter inventory
+
+`extract.mjs` implements the download/extraction adapter. All behavior used by
+this action is implemented and tested:
+
+| Contract                                  | Implementation and verification                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
+| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
+| SDK transport, retries and digest results | Raw download into an owned temporary directory; reject missing/extra files and digest mismatches. `scripts/artifact-transport.mjs` retries transient failures. The hosted roundtrip exercises the actual SDK.                        |
+| Complete extraction before success        | Await each file's streamed writer; return the destination only after extraction. The probe checks bytes immediately after return.                                                                                                    |
+| Bounded memory and ZIP64                  | Read a disk-backed Blob; decompress one entry at a time without workers or whole-archive buffering. The probe uses real ZIP64 metadata with small files.                                                                             |
+| Names and safety                          | Preserve binary, empty, nested and dot-prefixed files. Refuse traversal in either slash spelling, absolute and drive paths, and pre-existing destination links. Archive symlinks stay ordinary data files, as with the SDK's reader. |
+| Corruption and cleanup                    | Verify CRC32; propagate malformed archive, filesystem and transport errors. Remove only the owned download directory on success and failure.                                                                                         |
+
+Password-protected or split archives are not produced by this action and are
+outside its contract. Concurrent untrusted modification of the destination is
+not supported; jobs own their output directories.
+
+Run `npm ci --prefix .github/actions/artifact-transport --ignore-scripts`, then
+`node --pending-deprecation --throw-deprecation scripts/check-artifact-archive.mjs`.
+The probe exercises the real archive dependencies, glob exclusions, ZIP64,
+binary/empty/nested files, traversal, CRC failure, symlinks and cleanup. The
+`Artifact Transport Regression` job in `workflows.yml` additionally uploads and
+downloads bytes and a Pages tar file through GitHub. Deprecations fail these
+checks instead of being suppressed.
+
+Remove the glob override when its consumer ships a maintained compatible
+dependency. Remove the extraction adapter and reader pin when the official SDK
+provides a reader without runtime deprecations. Keep the local and hosted
+assertions when updating versions. All three npm locks are audited on every PR
+and on the weekly security schedule.

+name: 'Set up Docker Buildx (resilient)'
+description: >
+  Wrapper around docker/setup-buildx-action that first pre-pulls the pinned
+  BuildKit image with retries and exponential backoff, and — when Docker Hub
+  itself is unreachable — falls back to a pull-through registry mirror
+  (mirror.gcr.io by default) before re-tagging the image to its canonical
+  reference. Booting the docker-container driver otherwise pulls moby/buildkit
+  straight from Docker Hub, and a transient registry timeout there fails the
+  whole publish job (see issue #75, and the upstream investigations in
+  link-foundation/box issues #97 and #100). Seeding the image locally first
+  means the boot reuses the cached image instead of hitting the registry, and
+  the mirror fallback keeps the seed working even during a full Docker Hub
+  registry outage.
+inputs:
+  buildkit-image:
+    description: 'Pinned BuildKit image used by the docker-container driver.'
+    required: false
+    default: 'moby/buildkit:buildx-stable-1'
+  registry-mirror:
+    description: >
+      Pull-through Docker Hub mirror host used as a fallback when the canonical
+      registry (registry-1.docker.io) is unreachable. mirror.gcr.io is Google's
+      public pull-through cache of Docker Hub and is served from independent
+      infrastructure, so it typically stays reachable during Docker Hub
+      registry outages. Set to an empty string to disable the mirror fallback.
+    required: false
+    default: 'mirror.gcr.io'
+  verbose:
+    description: >
+      Set to "true" to enable shell tracing (set -x) in the pre-pull step for
+      debugging. Tracing is also enabled automatically when the workflow is run
+      with step debug logging (RUNNER_DEBUG=1).
+    required: false
+    default: 'false'
+runs:
+  using: 'composite'
+  steps:
+    - name: Pre-pull BuildKit image (retry + registry-mirror fallback)
+      shell: bash
+      env:
+        BUILDKIT_IMAGE: ${{ inputs.buildkit-image }}
+        REGISTRY_MIRROR: ${{ inputs.registry-mirror }}
+        VERBOSE: ${{ inputs.verbose }}
+      run: |
+        set -u
+        # Verbose/debug tracing: opt-in via input, or automatic when the run is
+        # started with "Enable debug logging" (RUNNER_DEBUG=1). Kept off by
+        # default so normal logs stay readable.
+        if [ "${VERBOSE}" = "true" ] || [ "${RUNNER_DEBUG:-}" = "1" ]; then
+          echo "==> Verbose tracing enabled"
+          set -x
+        fi
+
+        # Pull a reference with bounded retries and exponential backoff.
+        # Returns 0 on the first successful pull, non-zero if all attempts fail.
+        pull_with_retries() {
+          ref="$1"
+          # Attempts/backoff are overridable via env so the unit test can run
+          # fast; the CI defaults stay at 5 attempts / 5s exponential backoff.
+          attempts="${PREPULL_ATTEMPTS:-5}"
+          delay="${PREPULL_DELAY:-5}"
+          for attempt in $(seq 1 "$attempts"); do
+            echo "==> Pulling ${ref} (attempt ${attempt}/${attempts})..."
+            if docker pull "${ref}"; then
+              return 0
+            fi
+            if [ "$attempt" -lt "$attempts" ]; then
+              echo "==> Pull failed, waiting ${delay}s before next attempt..."
+              sleep "$delay"
+              delay=$((delay * 2))
+            fi
+          done
+          return 1
+        }
+
+        # 1) Canonical Docker Hub. The common transient-blip case recovers here.
+        if pull_with_retries "${BUILDKIT_IMAGE}"; then
+          echo "==> BuildKit image cached locally from canonical registry; boot will not need a registry pull"
+          exit 0
+        fi
+
+        # 2) Registry-mirror fallback. When Docker Hub's registry endpoint is
+        #    fully unreachable (issue #75 / box #100: registry-1.docker.io timed
+        #    out for ~2.5 minutes), the canonical pull above cannot recover no
+        #    matter how many times it retries. mirror.gcr.io is a pull-through
+        #    cache of Docker Hub on independent infrastructure, so it usually
+        #    still serves the image. We pull from there and re-tag to the
+        #    canonical reference so the docker-container driver boot finds it
+        #    locally and never touches the failing registry.
+        if [ -n "${REGISTRY_MIRROR}" ]; then
+          mirror_ref="${REGISTRY_MIRROR}/${BUILDKIT_IMAGE}"
+          echo "==> Canonical pull failed; trying registry mirror ${mirror_ref}"
+          if pull_with_retries "${mirror_ref}"; then
+            docker tag "${mirror_ref}" "${BUILDKIT_IMAGE}"
+            echo "==> BuildKit image cached locally via mirror and tagged as ${BUILDKIT_IMAGE}; boot will reuse it"
+            exit 0
+          fi
+          echo "==> Mirror pull from ${REGISTRY_MIRROR} also failed"
+        fi
+
+        # Non-fatal: fall through to setup-buildx, which will attempt its own
+        # pull during boot. This preserves the previous behaviour in the worst
+        # case while making the common transient-failure case recover.
+        echo "==> WARNING: could not pre-pull ${BUILDKIT_IMAGE} from canonical registry or mirror; letting setup-buildx try its own boot pull"
+
+    - name: Set up Docker Buildx
+      uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4
+      with:
+        driver-opts: image=${{ inputs.buildkit-image }}

+          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

+            git status --porcelain
+            exit 0
+          fi

+          # Do not add [skip ci]: a fallback PR needs its required checks.
+          git commit -m "chore(preview): regenerate example-app preview images"
+          if [[ -n "$RELEASE_PR_TOKEN" ]]; then
+            node scripts/push-main-with-rebase-retry.mjs origin main --label preview-images
+            echo "landed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+            exit 0
+          fi
+          echo "RELEASE_PR_TOKEN is not set: pushing with the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN."
+          if ! node scripts/push-main-with-rebase-retry.mjs origin main --label preview-images; then
+            echo "::error title=Preview images need RELEASE_PR_TOKEN::The preview images changed, but main refused a push with the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN (a ruleset requires a pull request, and pull requests opened by that token do not run checks). Add a fine-grained token with Contents and Pull requests read/write access as the RELEASE_PR_TOKEN secret at $SECRETS_URL and re-run this job, or run 'npm run example:web:preview-images' locally and commit docs/screenshots/example-app/*.png."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          echo "landed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+
+      - name: Upload screenshot failure artifacts
+        if: failure()
+        uses: ./.github/actions/artifact-transport
+        with:
+          name: preview-regen-failure-${{ github.run_id }}
+          path: docs/screenshots/example-app/
+          retention-days: 7
+          if-no-files-found: error
+
+      # One outcome, one message: report what actually happened instead of
+      # claiming a commit that a failed step never made.
+      - name: Summarize regeneration result
+        if: always()
+        env:
+          REGENERATE: ${{ steps.regenerate.outcome }}
+          DRIFT: ${{ steps.drift.outputs.drift }}
+          DRIFT_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.drift.outcome }}
+          COMMIT: ${{ steps.commit.outcome }}
+          LANDED: ${{ steps.commit.outputs.landed }}
+        run: |
+          if [[ "$REGENERATE" != "success" ]]; then
+            echo "Preview images were not regenerated (step outcome: ${REGENERATE:-not run})."
+          elif [[ "$DRIFT_OUTCOME" != "success" ]]; then
+            echo "Preview drift could not be checked (step outcome: ${DRIFT_OUTCOME:-not run})."
+          elif [[ "$DRIFT" == "false" ]]; then
+            echo "::notice::Preview images are already up to date."
+          elif [[ "$COMMIT" == "success" && "$LANDED" == "true" ]]; then
+            echo "::notice::Regenerated preview images were committed to main."
+          else
+            echo "Regenerated preview images differ but were not committed (commit outcome: ${COMMIT:-not run})."
+          fi
+
+  # Terminal status gate: runs even when the jobs above fail or are
+  # cancelled, and turns a `timeout-minutes` kill (reported as cancelled)
+  # into a red run. needs is derived and checked by the status-gate-coverage
+  # job in workflows.yml.
+  pipeline-status:
+    name: Pipeline Status
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-pipeline-status
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    # A status function is required: without one the gate inherits the
+    # implicit "every dependency succeeded" condition and is skipped in
+    # exactly the runs it exists to report.
+    if: >-
+      !cancelled()
+    needs:
+      - web-build
+      - pages-deploy
+      - desktop-package
+      - android-build
+      - ios-build
+      - preview-regen
+      - preview-tools
+    # actions: read lets the gate list this run's jobs and name the ones

+    permissions:
+      actions: read
+      contents: read
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Setup Node.js
+        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
+        with:
+          node-version: '24.x'
+
+      - name: Fail the run when a required job was cancelled or failed
+        env:
+          NEEDS_JSON: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          RUN_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
+          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && format('refs/pull/{0}/head', github.event.number) || github.ref }}
+        run: bash scripts/check-pipeline-status.sh

+name: JavaScript-first gate
+
+on:
+  workflow_call:
+    inputs:
+      source-sha:
+        description: Immutable forty-character commit SHA to validate, including release candidates
+        required: true
+        type: string
+      javascript-command:
+        description: Install dependencies and run the complete native JavaScript checks
+        required: true
+        type: string
+      parity-command:
+        description: Run the strict complete-feature parity inventory check
+        required: true
+        type: string
+      translation-command:
+        description: Regenerate from pinned source and reject target drift or carried code
+        required: true
+        type: string
+    outputs:
+      tested-sha:
+        description: Exact revision that passed all three prerequisite stages
+        value: ${{ jobs.javascript-first.outputs.tested-sha }}
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  javascript-first:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 30
+    outputs:
+      tested-sha: ${{ steps.revision.outputs.sha }}
+    steps:
+      - name: Validate requested revision
+        env:
+          EXPECTED_SHA: ${{ inputs.source-sha }}
+        run: |
+          [[ "$EXPECTED_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]
+      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ inputs.source-sha }}
+          persist-credentials: false
+      - name: Check exact checkout revision
+        env:
+          EXPECTED_SHA: ${{ inputs.source-sha }}
+        run: |
+          test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$EXPECTED_SHA"
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1
+        with:
+          node-version: '24'
+          # Caller-selected revisions must not populate the caller's cache scope.
+          package-manager-cache: false
+      - name: Native JavaScript checks
+        env:
+          CHECK_COMMAND: ${{ inputs.javascript-command }}
+        run: |
+          bash -e -o pipefail -c "$CHECK_COMMAND"
+      - name: Strict feature parity inventory
+        env:
+          CHECK_COMMAND: ${{ inputs.parity-command }}
+        run: |
+          bash -e -o pipefail -c "$CHECK_COMMAND"
+      - name: Deterministic regeneration check
+        env:
+          CHECK_COMMAND: ${{ inputs.translation-command }}
+        run: |
+          bash -e -o pipefail -c "$CHECK_COMMAND"
+      - name: Record successful revision
+        id: revision
+        env:
+          EXPECTED_SHA: ${{ inputs.source-sha }}
+        run: |
+          test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$EXPECTED_SHA"
+          git diff --exit-code
+          git diff --cached --exit-code
+          test -z "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)"
+          printf 'sha=%s\n' "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches:
+      - main
+    paths:
+      - '**.md'
+      - '**.html'
+      - '.github/workflows/links.yml'
+      - '.github/actions/artifact-transport/**'
+      - 'scripts/artifact-transport.mjs'
+      - 'scripts/artifact-files.mjs'
+      - '.lycheeignore'
+      - 'scripts/check-web-archive.mjs'
+      - 'scripts/lychee-report.mjs'
+      - 'scripts/recheck-broken-links.mjs'
+      - 'tests/fixtures/lychee-report.md'
+      - 'tests/links-workflow.test.js'
+      - 'tests/recheck-broken-links.test.js'
+  pull_request:
+    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
+    paths:
+      - '**.md'
+      - '**.html'
+      - '.github/workflows/links.yml'
+      - '.github/actions/artifact-transport/**'
+      - 'scripts/artifact-transport.mjs'
+      - 'scripts/artifact-files.mjs'
+      - '.lycheeignore'
+      - 'scripts/check-web-archive.mjs'
+      - 'scripts/lychee-report.mjs'
+      - 'scripts/recheck-broken-links.mjs'
+      - 'tests/fixtures/lychee-report.md'
+      - 'tests/links-workflow.test.js'
+      - 'tests/recheck-broken-links.test.js'
+  # External URLs rot without any commit here; recheck them weekly so a dead
+  # link is reported by this run instead of by the next unrelated docs PR.
+  schedule:
+    - cron: '0 6 * * 1'
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+# Least-privilege default; jobs escalate individually when needed.
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+# Provide Git config to actions/checkout itself; checkout runs git init before
+# any workflow step can configure Git.
+env:
+  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
+  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: init.defaultBranch
+  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main
+
+jobs:
+  link-checker:
+    name: Check Links
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    # Typical run: <1min with lychee cache. 10min prevents slow
+    # external hosts or Wayback Machine probes from hanging the workflow.
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-link-checker
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      # lychee keeps results for --max-cache-age 1d. Scoping the cache to the
+      # UTC day restores only a cache saved today, so lychee never has to
+      # discard a restored cache as "too old".
+      - name: Name today's link cache
+        id: link-cache
+        run: echo "day=$(date -u +%F)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+
+      - name: Restore link cache

+        with:
+          path: .lycheecache

+          restore-keys: cache-lychee-${{ runner.os }}-${{ steps.link-cache.outputs.day }}-

+        uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2
+        with:
+          # Check all Markdown and HTML files
+          # Exclude case-studies directory - these are research documents from
+          # external repos with references to files and issues that don't exist
+          # in this repository (similar exclusion pattern as eslint.config.js)
+          # Exclude the Vite source HTML because its root-relative app asset
+          # URLs are only valid when served by Vite.
+          # Exclude tests/fixtures - the captured lychee reports there contain
+          # deliberately broken links used as parser test input.
+          args: >-
+            --verbose
+            --no-progress
+            --cache
+            --max-cache-age 1d
+            --max-retries 3
+            --timeout 30
+            --hidden
+            --extensions md,html
+            --exclude-path docs/case-studies
+            --exclude-path dev/log
+            --exclude-path examples/universal-app/index.html
+            --exclude-path tests/fixtures
+            .

+          fail: false
+          # Output file for broken links report (used by check-web-archive.mjs)
+          output: lychee/out.md
+          # Write a job summary
+          jobSummary: true
+        env:
+          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+
+      - name: Re-check transient link failures
+        # Retry transport errors, 429, and 5xx within a shared budget.
+        # GitHub blob/tree pages also use the authenticated contents API.
+        if: steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != 0
+        id: recheck
+        run: node scripts/recheck-broken-links.mjs
+        env:
+          LYCHEE_OUTPUT: lychee/out.md
+          RECOVERED_OUTPUT: lychee/recovered.txt
+          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+
+      - name: Check broken links against Web Archive
+        # `!= 'true'`, never `== 'false'`: a skipped re-check leaves the
+        # output empty, and only the != form fails safe.
+        if: >-
+          steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != 0 &&
+          steps.recheck.outputs.all_recovered != 'true'
+        id: webarchive
+        run: node scripts/check-web-archive.mjs
+        env:
+          LYCHEE_OUTPUT: lychee/out.md
+          RECOVERED_URLS: lychee/recovered.txt
+          LYCHEE_EXIT_CODE: ${{ steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code }}
+
+      - name: Upload broken-link diagnostics
+        if: "!cancelled() && steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != '0'"
+        uses: ./.github/actions/artifact-transport
+        with:
+          name: lychee-report
+          path: lychee/
+          required-file: lychee/out.md
+          if-no-files-found: error
+
+      - name: Fail if broken links were found
+        if: >-
+          !cancelled() &&
+          steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != 0 &&
+          steps.recheck.outputs.all_recovered != 'true'
+        run: |
+          echo "::error::Broken live links were detected."
+          echo ""
+          echo "What happened:"
+          echo "  lychee found one or more broken links in the *.md and *.html files of this repository."
+          echo "  An archive is a suggested replacement; it does not make the live link valid."
+          echo ""
+          echo "How to fix:"
+          echo "  1. Review the 'Check links with lychee' step above for a full list of broken links."
+          echo "  2. For links marked with a '::notice::' annotation above, a Web Archive replacement exists."
+          echo "     Replace those broken links with the suggested archive.org URL."
+          echo "  3. For links with no archive version, either:"
+          echo "     a. Find an updated URL that points to the same or equivalent content."
+          echo "     b. Remove the link if the content is no longer relevant."
+          echo "     c. Add the URL to .lycheeignore if it is a known false positive."
+          echo ""
+          echo "Report location: lychee/out.md (download the lychee-report workflow artifact)."

+  # cancelled, and turns a `timeout-minutes` kill (reported as cancelled)
+  # into a red run. needs is derived and checked by the status-gate-coverage
+  # job in workflows.yml.
+  pipeline-status:
+    name: Pipeline Status
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-pipeline-status
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    # A status function is required: without one the gate inherits the

+    if: >-

+    # actions: read lets the gate list this run's jobs and name the ones

+    permissions:

+      contents: read

+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Setup Node.js
+        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
+        with:
+          node-version: '24.x'
+
+      - name: Fail the run when a required job was cancelled or failed
+        env:
+          NEEDS_JSON: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          RUN_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
+          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && format('refs/pull/{0}/head', github.event.number) || github.ref }}
+        run: bash scripts/check-pipeline-status.sh

+name: Checks and release
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches:
+      - main
+  pull_request:
+    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
+  # Manual release support - consolidated here to work with npm trusted publishing
+  # npm only allows ONE workflow file as trusted publisher, so all publishing
+  # must go through this workflow (release.yml)
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      release_mode:
+        description: 'Manual release mode'
+        required: true
+        type: choice
+        default: 'instant'
+        options:
+          - instant
+          - changeset-pr
+      bump_type:
+        description: 'Manual release type'
+        default: patch
+        required: true
+        type: choice
+        options:
+          - patch
+          - minor
+          - major
+      description:
+        description: 'Manual release description (optional)'
+        required: false
+        type: string
+
+# Least-privilege default for the highest-value token in the repository.
+# Every job starts read-only; the publishing jobs escalate individually.
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+# Provide Git config to actions/checkout itself; checkout runs git init before
+# any workflow step can configure Git.
+env:
+  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
+  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: init.defaultBranch
+  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main
+
+jobs:
+  # === DETECT CHANGES - determines which jobs should run ===
+  detect-changes:
+    name: Detect Changes
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    # Typical run: ~6s. Cap at 5min so a hung detection step
+    # surfaces quickly instead of stalling the whole pipeline.
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    # Job-level permissions replace the workflow defaults for this job.
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+      # The detector asks the Actions API whether the previous head of the
+      # branch already passed this workflow, so a docs-only push can trust
+      # its incremental range.
+      actions: read
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-detect-changes
+      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
+    if: github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch'
+    outputs:
+      js-changed: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.js-changed }}
+      docs-changed: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.docs-changed }}
+      any-code-changed: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.any-code-changed }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 0
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Detect changes
+        id: changes
+        env:
+          GITHUB_BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
+          GITHUB_BEFORE_SHA: ${{ github.event.before }}
+          GITHUB_AFTER_SHA: ${{ github.event.after }}
+          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+          GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF: ${{ github.workflow_ref }}
+        run: node scripts/detect-code-changes.mjs
+
+  # === FAST CHECKS - run before slow tests for fastest feedback ===
+  # See: hive-mind CI/CD best practices principle #5 (fast-fail job ordering)
+
+  # Syntax check every tracked JavaScript file recursively with node --check.
+  test-compilation:
+    name: Test Compilation
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    # Typical run: <10s. Tight cap fails fast on syntax-check hangs.
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-test-compilation
+      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
+    needs: [detect-changes]
+    if: |
+      !cancelled() &&
+      (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || needs.detect-changes.outputs.js-changed == 'true')
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Setup Node.js
+        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
+        with:
+          node-version: '24.x'
+
+      - name: Check tracked JavaScript syntax
+        run: bash scripts/check-mjs-syntax.sh
+
+  # Enforce 1500-line limit on .mjs files and release.yml
+  check-file-line-limits:
+    name: Check File Line Limits
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    # Typical run: <10s. This job only walks tracked files and counts lines.
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-check-file-line-limits
+      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
+    needs: [detect-changes]
+    if: |
+      !cancelled() &&
+      (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
+      needs.detect-changes.outputs.docs-changed == 'true' ||
+      needs.detect-changes.outputs.any-code-changed == 'true')
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 0
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Simulate fresh merge with base branch (PR only)
+        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
+        env:
+          BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
+        run: bash scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh
+
+      # Enforces the 1500-line limit on JavaScript (.js/.mjs/.cjs) and
+      # Markdown (.md) files plus release.yml. This is the single source
+      # of truth for the line limit; validate-docs no longer re-checks it.
+      - name: Check file line limits
+        run: bash scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh
+
+  # === VERSION CHANGE CHECK ===
+  # Prohibit manual version changes in package.json - versions should only be changed by CI/CD
+  version-check:
+    name: Check for Manual Version Changes
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    # Typical run: ~6s. Read-only package.json diff inspection.
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-version-check
+      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
+    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'

+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 0
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Check for version changes in package.json

+          GITHUB_HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}
+          GITHUB_BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
+          GITHUB_BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
+          GITHUB_HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
+          RELEASE_PR_ACTOR: ${{ vars.RELEASE_PR_ACTOR }}
+        run: node scripts/check-version.mjs
+
+  # === CHANGESET CHECK - only runs on PRs with code changes ===
+  # Docs-only PRs (./docs folder, markdown files) don't require changesets
+  changeset-check:
+    name: Check for Changesets
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    # Typical run: <30s including npm ci. 10min covers cold runners.
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-changeset-check
+      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
+    needs: [detect-changes]
+    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.detect-changes.outputs.any-code-changed == 'true'
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 0
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Setup Node.js
+        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
+        with:
+          node-version: '24.x'
+
+      - name: Install dependencies
+        run: npm ci
+
+      - name: Check for changesets
+        env:
+          # Pass PR context to the validation script
+          GITHUB_BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
+          GITHUB_BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
+          GITHUB_HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}
+          GITHUB_HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
+          RELEASE_PR_ACTOR: ${{ vars.RELEASE_PR_ACTOR }}
+          PR_AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}
+        run: |
+          # Run changeset validation script
+          # This validates that exactly ONE changeset was ADDED by this PR
+          # Pre-existing changesets from other merged PRs are ignored
+          node scripts/validate-changeset.mjs
+
+  # === LINT AND FORMAT CHECK ===
+  # Lint runs independently of changeset-check - it's a fast check that should always run
+  # See: https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/1024 for why this dependency was removed
+  # IMPORTANT: ESLint includes max-lines rule (1500 lines) to ensure files stay maintainable
+  # See docs/case-studies/issue-23 for why fresh merge simulation is critical
+  lint:
+    name: Lint and Format Check
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    # Typical run: <1min including install, ESLint, Prettier, jscpd,
+    # and secretlint. 10min protects against a hung lint plugin.
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-lint
+      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
+    needs: [detect-changes]
+    if: |
+      !cancelled() &&
+      (
+        github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
+        needs.detect-changes.outputs.docs-changed == 'true' ||
+        needs.detect-changes.outputs.any-code-changed == 'true'
+      )
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          # For PRs, fetch enough history to merge with base branch
+          fetch-depth: 0
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Simulate fresh merge with base branch (PR only)
+        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
+        env:
+          BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
+        run: bash scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh
+
+      - name: Setup Node.js
+        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
+        with:
+          node-version: '24.x'
+
+      - name: Check for secrets
+        run: npx --yes -p secretlint@13.0.7 -p @secretlint/secretlint-rule-preset-recommend@13.0.7 secretlint "**/*"
+
+      - name: Install dependencies
+        run: npm ci
+
+      # Exercise versioning without credentials, even if release-preflight fails.
+      # Restore consumed changesets and metadata on success or failure so lint
+      # checks the fresh merge rather than generated release files.
+      - name: Dry-run release versioning (PR only)
+        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
+        env:
+          npm_config_offline: 'true'
+          npm_config_ignore_scripts: 'true'
+        run: |
+          trap 'git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree -- .' EXIT
+          npm run changeset:version
+          git status --short
+
+      - name: Run ESLint
+        env:
+          LINT_ALL_WARNINGS: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' && '1' || '0' }}
+        run: npm run lint
+
+      - name: Check formatting
+        run: npm run format:check
+
+      - name: Check code duplication
+        run: npm run check:duplication
+
+  # Test matrix: 3 runtimes (Node.js, Bun, Deno) x 3 OS (Ubuntu, macOS, Windows)
+  # IMPORTANT: Tests must validate the ACTUAL merge result, not a stale merge preview.
+  # See docs/case-studies/issue-23 for why this is critical.
+  # Fast-fail: slow test matrix only runs after fast checks pass (hive-mind principle #5)
+  test:
+    name: Test runtimes
+    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
+    # Typical run: <1min per runtime/OS on warm runners, with Windows
+    # sometimes slower on cold starts. Each test step owns an explicit
+    # budget below (see scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh); this cap is
+    # only the backstop behind those budgets, sized so the budgets always
+    # expire first. A job killed by timeout-minutes reports *cancelled*,
+    # which hides the failure -- see docs/CI-TIMEOUT-BUDGETS.md.
+    timeout-minutes: 15
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-test-${{ matrix.runtime }}-${{ matrix.os }}
+      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
+    needs:
+      [
+        detect-changes,
+        changeset-check,
+        test-compilation,
+        lint,
+        check-file-line-limits,
+      ]
+    # Use !cancelled() instead of always() so cancellation propagates correctly (hive-mind issue #1278)
+    # Run for relevant code/package/workflow changes, or for an instant manual
+    # release. Skipped fast checks count as non-failures only after one of
+    # those positive gates passes.
+    if: |
+      !cancelled() &&
+      (
+        needs.detect-changes.outputs.any-code-changed == 'true' ||
+        (
+          github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
+          github.event.inputs.release_mode == 'instant'
+        )
+      ) &&
+      (needs.changeset-check.result == 'success' || needs.changeset-check.result == 'skipped') &&
+      (needs.test-compilation.result == 'success' || needs.test-compilation.result == 'skipped') &&
+      (needs.lint.result == 'success' || needs.lint.result == 'skipped') &&
+      (needs.check-file-line-limits.result == 'success' || needs.check-file-line-limits.result == 'skipped')
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix:
+        os: [ubuntu-24.04, macos-15, windows-2025]
+        runtime: [node, bun, deno]
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          # For PRs, fetch enough history to merge with base branch
+          fetch-depth: 0
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Simulate fresh merge with base branch (PR only)
+        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
+        env:
+          BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
+        shell: bash
+        run: bash scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh
+
+      # Every runtime leg also exercises native Node fixtures (Changesets,
+      # pipeline scripts and the Pages adapter), so each leg pins Node 24 and
+      # installs the owning locks explicitly instead of relying on packages
+      # another runtime happened to resolve.
+      - name: Setup Node.js
+        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
+        with:
+          node-version: '24.x'
+
+      - name: Install dependencies (runtime tests and native fixtures)
+        run: npm ci
+
+      - name: Install native CI adapter dependencies
+        run: npm ci --prefix .github/actions/artifact-transport --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
+
+      - name: Run tests (Node.js)
+        if: matrix.runtime == 'node'
+        shell: bash
+        run: bash scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh 300 "Node.js test suite" npm test
+
+      - name: Setup Bun
+        if: matrix.runtime == 'bun'
+        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
+        with:
+          bun-version: '1.x'
+
+      - name: Run tests (Bun)
+        if: matrix.runtime == 'bun'
+        shell: bash
+        # --timeout caps an *individual* test at 30s, matching Node's
+        # --test-timeout budget while leaving headroom for cold runners.
+        # It is a per-test bound and does not bound the suite: 25 tests of
+        # 29s each pass every per-test check. The suite budget below is
+        # what bounds the whole run.
+        run: bash scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh 200 "Bun test suite" bun test --timeout 30000
+
+      - name: Setup Deno
+        if: matrix.runtime == 'deno'
+        uses: denoland/setup-deno@22d081ff2d3a40755e97629de92e3bcbfa7cf2ed # v2.0.5
+        with:
+          deno-version: v2.x
+

+      # ci does for the other runtimes. --no-run executes no test assertions,
+      # so the 100s suite budget below still measures every acceptance test.
+      - name: Prepare Deno test dependencies
+        if: matrix.runtime == 'deno'

+
+      - name: Run tests (Deno)
+        if: matrix.runtime == 'deno'

+
+  # === DOCKER IMAGE BUILD CHECK (pull requests) ===
+  # Builds the Dockerfile without pushing so a broken image fails the pull
+  # request instead of surfacing only after publish (issue #106).
+  # push: false + load: true keeps this working for fork pull requests,
+  # which have no registry credentials. Skipped when no Dockerfile exists.
+  docker-build:
+    name: Docker Image Build Check
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    # Typical run: a few minutes with a warm GHA layer cache. 30min covers
+    # a cold, uncached build without allowing a 6h hang.
+    timeout-minutes: 30
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-docker-build
+      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
+    needs: [detect-changes]
+    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.detect-changes.outputs.any-code-changed == 'true'
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+    env:
+      DOCKER_CONTEXT: ${{ vars.DOCKER_CONTEXT }}
+      DOCKERFILE: ${{ vars.DOCKERFILE }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Check Docker build configuration
+        id: docker_config
+        run: node scripts/check-docker-build.mjs
+
+      - name: Set up Docker Buildx (resilient)
+        if: steps.docker_config.outputs.enabled == 'true'
+        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-buildx-resilient
+
+      - name: Build Docker image (no push)
+        if: steps.docker_config.outputs.enabled == 'true'
+        # A `uses:` step cannot be wrapped by run-with-budget-warning.sh, so
+        # it declares its deadline with a step-level timeout-minutes: an
+        # exhausted step budget fails the step, while an exhausted job cap
+        # only cancels the job.
+        timeout-minutes: 20
+        uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
+        with:
+          context: ${{ steps.docker_config.outputs.context }}
+          file: ${{ steps.docker_config.outputs.dockerfile }}
+          push: false
+          load: true
+          tags: pr-check:${{ github.sha }}
+          # Scoped so this build cannot overwrite or be overwritten by the
+          # unscoped default `buildkit` scope: the GitHub Actions cache is a
+          # 10 GB repository-wide pool with LRU eviction, and unscoped
+          # mode=max exports of every intermediate layer crowd out the caches
+          # the rest of the pipeline reads.
+          cache-from: type=gha,scope=docker-image
+          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=docker-image
+
+  # === DOCUMENTATION VALIDATION ===
+  # Validate documentation files when docs change (hive-mind principle #12)
+  validate-docs:
+    name: Validate Documentation
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    # Typical run: <10s. Pure shell checks over documentation files.
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-validate-docs
+      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
+    needs: [detect-changes]
+    if: |
+      needs.detect-changes.outputs.docs-changed == 'true'
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+

+      # limit) are enforced by the check-file-line-limits job, which scans
+      # every .md file. This job validates that the required documents
+      # exist AND still carry the sections readers depend on -- a deleted
+      # section is an ordinary diff hunk, and is exactly what review skims
+      # past. The requirement table lives in
+      # scripts/check-required-docs.sh; `--list` prints it for tests and
+      # reviewers.
+      - name: Check required documentation sections
+        run: bash scripts/check-required-docs.sh
+
+  # Principle 16 of the shared CI/CD best practices: prove the release
+  # credentials can write before the expensive jobs spend their minutes
+  # (issues #176, #181). A non-empty secret proves nothing -- an expired
+  # token is non-empty -- and a login proves authentication, not
+  # authorisation, so scripts/preflight-credentials.sh probes with an
+  # attempted write: a refused credential fails the run seconds in instead
+  # of surfacing as a registry error after the matrix.
+  release-preflight:
+    name: Release Preflight
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 5

+      contents: read
+      # The runner injects ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL only when the job may
+      # mint OIDC tokens. npm publishes with provenance, so its absence --
+      # mirrored in the publishing jobs' permission envelope -- is itself the
+      # finding.
+      id-token: write

+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false

+            ${{
+              (
+                (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') ||
+                (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.release_mode == 'instant')

+          DOCKERHUB_IMAGE: ${{ vars.DOCKERHUB_IMAGE }}
+          DOCKERHUB_USERNAME: ${{ vars.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
+          DOCKERHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}
+        run: bash scripts/preflight-credentials.sh
+
+  # Release - only runs on main after tests pass (for push events)
+  release:
+    name: Release
+    needs:
+      [
+        detect-changes,
+        test-compilation,
+        check-file-line-limits,
+        version-check,
+        changeset-check,
+        lint,
+        test,
+        docker-build,
+        validate-docs,
+        release-preflight,
+      ]

+    # with headroom for install/smoke steps under the 70% budget policy.
+    timeout-minutes: 65
+    concurrency:
+      group: main-writer-${{ github.repository }}-main
+      cancel-in-progress: false
+      queue: max
+    # Use !cancelled() instead of always() so cancellation propagates correctly (hive-mind issue #1278)
+    # This is needed because lint/test jobs have a transitive dependency on changeset-check
+    if: |
+      !cancelled() &&
+      github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
+      github.event_name == 'push' &&
+      needs.release-preflight.result == 'success' &&
+      needs.lint.result == 'success' &&
+      needs.test.result == 'success' &&
+      !contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') &&
+      !contains(needs.*.result, 'cancelled')

+    # Permissions required for npm OIDC trusted publishing
+    permissions:
+      contents: write
+      pull-requests: write
+      checks: write
+      id-token: write
+    outputs:
+      published: ${{ steps.publish.outputs.published }}
+      published_version: ${{ steps.publish.outputs.published_version }}
+    steps:

+      # .git/config: scripts/version-and-commit.mjs runs
+      # `git push origin main` to publish the version bump, which needs the
+      # token wired into the remote. Every other checkout in this
+      # repository sets persist-credentials: false.
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: true
+          fetch-depth: 0
+
+      - name: Setup Node.js
+        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
+        with:
+          node-version: '24.x'
+          registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'
+
+      - name: Remove deprecated npm auth config
+        run: node scripts/sanitize-npm-userconfig.mjs
+

+      # detected package manager, and a foreign lockfile at the root

+      # declares the manager. The requirement table lives in the script.
+      - name: Check package manager declaration and lockfiles

+
+      - name: Install dependencies
+        run: bash scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh 240 "Release dependency install" npm ci
+

+        run: node scripts/setup-npm.mjs
+
+      - name: Check for changesets
+        id: check_changesets
+        run: node scripts/check-changesets.mjs
+

+          HAS_CHANGESETS: ${{ steps.check_changesets.outputs.has_changesets }}

+
+      - name: Merge multiple changesets

+          echo "Multiple changesets detected, merging..."
+          node scripts/merge-changesets.mjs
+

+        if: steps.check_changesets.outputs.has_changesets == 'true'

+        env:
+          # Prefer the dedicated actor when configured. Otherwise the built-in
+          # token attests a metadata-only version commit after parent validation.
+          RELEASE_PR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PR_TOKEN }}
+          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+          RELEASE_METADATA_PATHS: ${{ vars.RELEASE_METADATA_PATHS }}

+          steps.version.outputs.version_committed == 'true' ||
+          steps.version.outputs.already_released == 'true' ||

+        # first publish returns E404 because a trusted publisher can only be
+        # configured for a package that already exists). When NPM_TOKEN is set,
+        # the first publish succeeds; once the package exists and a trusted
+        # publisher is configured, OIDC takes over and the token can be removed.
+        # See issue #77.
+        env:
+          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
+        run: bash scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh 1800 "npm publish and registry verification" node scripts/publish-to-npm.mjs --should-pull
+
+      - name: Smoke-test published npm package
+        if: steps.publish.outputs.published == 'true'
+        env:
+          PACKAGE_VERSION: ${{ steps.publish.outputs.published_version }}
+        run: bash scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh 600 "npm package smoke test" node scripts/smoke-test-package.mjs --package-version "$PACKAGE_VERSION"
+
+      - name: Create GitHub Release
+        if: steps.publish.outputs.published == 'true'
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+          PACKAGE_VERSION: ${{ steps.publish.outputs.published_version }}
+          REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
+        run: node scripts/create-github-release.mjs --release-version "$PACKAGE_VERSION" --repository "$REPOSITORY"
+
+      - name: Format GitHub release notes
+        if: steps.publish.outputs.published == 'true'
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+          PACKAGE_VERSION: ${{ steps.publish.outputs.published_version }}
+          REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
+          COMMIT_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}

+  # Manual Instant Release - triggered via workflow_dispatch with instant mode
+  # This job is in release.yml because npm trusted publishing
+  # only allows one workflow file to be registered as a trusted publisher
+  instant-release:
+    name: Instant Release

+    needs:

+        detect-changes,
+        test-compilation,
+        check-file-line-limits,
+        version-check,
+        changeset-check,
+        lint,
+        test,
+        docker-build,
+        validate-docs,
+        release-preflight,
+      ]

+      !cancelled() &&
+      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
+      github.event.inputs.release_mode == 'instant' &&
+      needs.release-preflight.result == 'success' &&
+      needs.lint.result == 'success' &&
+      needs.test.result == 'success' &&
+      !contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') &&
+      !contains(needs.*.result, 'cancelled')

+    # Same publish envelope as the automated release path.
+    timeout-minutes: 65
+    concurrency:
+      group: main-writer-${{ github.repository }}-main
+      cancel-in-progress: false
+      queue: max
+    # Permissions required for npm OIDC trusted publishing
+    permissions:
+      contents: write
+      pull-requests: write
+      checks: write
+      id-token: write
+    outputs:
+      published: ${{ steps.publish.outputs.published }}
+      published_version: ${{ steps.publish.outputs.published_version }}
+    steps:
+      # The second checkout in this workflow that keeps credentials in
+      # .git/config: scripts/version-and-commit.mjs pushes the version
+      # commit to main, which needs the token wired into the remote.
+      # Every other checkout in this repository sets
+      # persist-credentials: false.
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: true
+          fetch-depth: 0
+
+      - name: Setup Node.js
+        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
+        with:
+          node-version: '24.x'
+          registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'
+
+      - name: Remove deprecated npm auth config
+        run: node scripts/sanitize-npm-userconfig.mjs
+
+      - name: Install dependencies
+        run: npm ci
+
+      - name: Update npm for OIDC trusted publishing
+        run: node scripts/setup-npm.mjs
+
+      - name: Version packages and commit to main
+        id: version
+        env:
+          BUMP_TYPE: ${{ github.event.inputs.bump_type }}
+          RELEASE_DESCRIPTION: ${{ github.event.inputs.description }}
+          # See the release job above (issues #143, #192, and #196).
+          RELEASE_PR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PR_TOKEN }}
+          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+          RELEASE_METADATA_PATHS: ${{ vars.RELEASE_METADATA_PATHS }}
+        run: node scripts/version-and-commit.mjs --mode instant --bump-type "$BUMP_TYPE" --description "$RELEASE_DESCRIPTION"
+

+        # Run if version was committed OR if a previous attempt already committed (for re-runs)
+        if: steps.version.outputs.version_committed == 'true' || steps.version.outputs.already_released == 'true'
+        id: publish
+        # Optional NPM_TOKEN bootstrap fallback; OIDC trusted publishing is used
+        # when the secret is unset. See the release job above for details (#77).
+        env:
+          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
+        run: bash scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh 1800 "npm publish and registry verification" node scripts/publish-to-npm.mjs
+
+      - name: Smoke-test published npm package
+        if: steps.publish.outputs.published == 'true'
+        env:
+          PACKAGE_VERSION: ${{ steps.publish.outputs.published_version }}
+        run: bash scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh 600 "npm package smoke test" node scripts/smoke-test-package.mjs --package-version "$PACKAGE_VERSION"
+
+      - name: Create GitHub Release
+        if: steps.publish.outputs.published == 'true'
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+          PACKAGE_VERSION: ${{ steps.publish.outputs.published_version }}
+          REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
+        run: node scripts/create-github-release.mjs --release-version "$PACKAGE_VERSION" --repository "$REPOSITORY"
+
+      - name: Format GitHub release notes
+        if: steps.publish.outputs.published == 'true'
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+          PACKAGE_VERSION: ${{ steps.publish.outputs.published_version }}
+          REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
+          COMMIT_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
+        run: node scripts/format-github-release.mjs --release-version "$PACKAGE_VERSION" --repository "$REPOSITORY" --commit-sha "$COMMIT_SHA"
+
+  # Optional Docker Hub publishing for packages that also ship Docker images.
+  # Set vars.DOCKERHUB_IMAGE to enable this path, then configure
+  # vars.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME and secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN.
+  docker-publish-config:
+    name: Configure Docker Hub Publish
+    needs: [release, instant-release, release-preflight]
+    timeout-minutes: 45
+    concurrency:
+      group: main-writer-${{ github.repository }}-main
+      cancel-in-progress: false
+      queue: max
+    if: |
+      !cancelled() &&
+      needs.release-preflight.result == 'success' &&
+      (
+        (needs.release.result == 'success' && needs.release.outputs.published == 'true') ||
+        (needs.instant-release.result == 'success' && needs.instant-release.outputs.published == 'true')
+      )
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+    outputs:
+      context: ${{ steps.docker_config.outputs.context }}
+      dockerfile: ${{ steps.docker_config.outputs.dockerfile }}
+      enabled: ${{ steps.docker_config.outputs.enabled }}
+      image: ${{ steps.docker_config.outputs.image }}
+      version: ${{ steps.release_version.outputs.version }}
+    env:
+      DOCKER_CONTEXT: ${{ vars.DOCKER_CONTEXT }}
+      DOCKERFILE: ${{ vars.DOCKERFILE }}
+      DOCKERHUB_IMAGE: ${{ vars.DOCKERHUB_IMAGE }}
+      DOCKERHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}
+      DOCKERHUB_USERNAME: ${{ vars.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
+      RELEASE_VERSION: ${{ needs.release.outputs.published_version || needs.instant-release.outputs.published_version }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Check Docker publish configuration
+        id: docker_config
+        run: node scripts/check-docker-publish.mjs
+
+      - name: Export release version
+        id: release_version
+        env:
+          VERSION: ${{ env.RELEASE_VERSION }}
+        run: echo "version=${VERSION}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+
+      - name: Wait for npm package availability before Docker publish
+        if: steps.docker_config.outputs.enabled == 'true'
+        env:
+          VERSION: ${{ env.RELEASE_VERSION }}
+        run: bash scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh 1800 "Docker npm availability wait" node scripts/wait-for-npm.mjs --release-version "${VERSION}"
+
+  # Build each architecture on a native runner. Each build is pushed by digest;
+  # docker-publish combines those immutable digests into the release tags.
+  docker-publish-build:
+    name: Build Docker Image
+    needs: [docker-publish-config]
+    if: needs.docker-publish-config.outputs.enabled == 'true'
+    timeout-minutes: 30
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix:
+        include:
+          - platform: linux/amd64
+            runner: ubuntu-24.04
+          - platform: linux/arm64
+            runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
+    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Build and push platform image by digest
+        id: build
+        # Step-level budget below the job's timeout-minutes backstop; see
+        # docs/CI-TIMEOUT-BUDGETS.md.
+        timeout-minutes: 20
+        uses: ./.github/actions/publish-dockerhub
+        with:
+          context: ${{ needs.docker-publish-config.outputs.context }}
+          file: ${{ needs.docker-publish-config.outputs.dockerfile }}
+          image: ${{ needs.docker-publish-config.outputs.image }}
+          platform: ${{ matrix.platform }}
+          token: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}
+          username: ${{ vars.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
+          version: ${{ needs.docker-publish-config.outputs.version }}
+
+      - name: Export image digest
+        env:
+          DIGEST: ${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}
+        run: |
+          mkdir -p /tmp/digests
+          touch "/tmp/digests/${DIGEST#sha256:}"
+
+      - name: Upload image digest
+        uses: ./.github/actions/artifact-transport
+        with:
+          name: docker-digest-${{ strategy.job-index }}
+          path: /tmp/digests/*
+          if-no-files-found: error
+          retention-days: 1
+
+  docker-publish:
+    name: Optional Docker Hub Publish
+    needs: [docker-publish-config, docker-publish-build]
+    if: needs.docker-publish-build.result == 'success'
+    timeout-minutes: 30
+    concurrency:
+      group: main-writer-${{ github.repository }}-main
+      cancel-in-progress: false
+      queue: max
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Set up Docker Buildx (resilient)
+        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-buildx-resilient
+
+      - name: Log in to Docker Hub
+        uses: docker/login-action@v4
+        with:
+          username: ${{ vars.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
+          password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}
+
+      - name: Download image digests
+        uses: ./.github/actions/artifact-transport
+        env:
+          NODE_OPTIONS: --pending-deprecation --throw-deprecation
+        with:
+          path: /tmp/digests
+          pattern: docker-digest-*
+          mode: download
+
+      - name: Create multi-architecture manifest
+        working-directory: /tmp/digests
+        env:
+          IMAGE: ${{ needs.docker-publish-config.outputs.image }}
+          VERSION: ${{ needs.docker-publish-config.outputs.version }}
+        run: |
+          # One argument per digest. An array keeps the expansion explicit
+          # instead of relying on word splitting of a command substitution.
+          mapfile -t digests < <(printf "${IMAGE}@sha256:%s\n" *)
+          if [[ "${#digests[@]}" -ne 2 ]]; then
+            echo "Expected 2 platform digests, found ${#digests[@]}." >&2
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          docker buildx imagetools create \
+            --tag "${IMAGE}:latest" \
+            --tag "${IMAGE}:${VERSION}" \
+            "${digests[@]}"
+
+      - name: Verify published multi-architecture manifests
+        env:
+          IMAGE: ${{ needs.docker-publish-config.outputs.image }}
+          VERSION: ${{ needs.docker-publish-config.outputs.version }}
+        run: |
+          for tag in latest "${VERSION}"; do
+            if ! manifest="$(docker buildx imagetools inspect "${IMAGE}:${tag}")"; then
+              echo "Unable to read back published manifest ${IMAGE}:${tag}" >&2
+              exit 1
+            fi
+            for platform in linux/amd64 linux/arm64; do
+              if ! grep -Eq "Platform:[[:space:]]+${platform}" <<<"${manifest}"; then
+                echo "Published manifest ${IMAGE}:${tag} is missing ${platform}" >&2
+                exit 1
+              fi
+            done
+          done
+
+  # Manual Changeset PR - creates a pull request with the changeset for review
+  changeset-pr:
+    name: Create Changeset PR
+    # PR creation does not publish, but it must still pass the fast lint gate.
+    needs: [lint]
+    if: |
+      !cancelled() &&
+      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
+      github.event.inputs.release_mode == 'changeset-pr' &&
+      needs.lint.result == 'success'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    # PR creation only: install, create a changeset, format, and open a PR.
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    concurrency:
+      group: main-writer-${{ github.repository }}-main
+      cancel-in-progress: false
+      queue: max
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+    steps:
+      # peter-evans/create-pull-request receives the dedicated token directly;
+      # dependency installation does not need a credential in .git/config.
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+          fetch-depth: 0
+
+      - name: Require release pull-request token
+        env:
+          RELEASE_PR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PR_TOKEN }}
+        run: |
+          if [[ -z "$RELEASE_PR_TOKEN" ]]; then
+            echo "::error::RELEASE_PR_TOKEN is required to create a changeset pull request."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+
+      - name: Setup Node.js
+        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
+        with:
+          node-version: '24.x'
+
+      - name: Install dependencies
+        run: npm ci
+
+      - name: Create changeset file
+        env:
+          BUMP_TYPE: ${{ github.event.inputs.bump_type }}
+          RELEASE_DESCRIPTION: ${{ github.event.inputs.description }}
+        run: node scripts/create-manual-changeset.mjs --bump-type "$BUMP_TYPE" --description "$RELEASE_DESCRIPTION"
+
+      - name: Format changeset with Prettier
+        run: |
+          # Run Prettier on the changeset file to ensure it matches project style
+          npx prettier --write ".changeset/*.md"
+
+          echo "Formatted changeset files"
+
+      - name: Create Pull Request
+        uses: peter-evans/create-pull-request@5f6978faf089d4d20b00c7766989d076bb2fc7f1 # v8.1.1
+        with:
+          # The built-in token suppresses pull_request workflows; use the same
+          # dedicated automation actor as the release fallback (issue #192).
+          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PR_TOKEN }}
+          commit-message: 'chore: add changeset for manual ${{ github.event.inputs.bump_type }} release'
+          branch: changeset-manual-release-${{ github.run_id }}
+          delete-branch: true
+          title: 'chore: manual ${{ github.event.inputs.bump_type }} release'
+          body: |
+            ## Manual Release Request
+
+            This PR was created by a manual workflow trigger to prepare a **${{ github.event.inputs.bump_type }}** release.
+
+            ### Release Details
+            - **Type:** ${{ github.event.inputs.bump_type }}
+            - **Description:** ${{ github.event.inputs.description || 'Manual release' }}
+            - **Triggered by:** @${{ github.actor }}
+
+            ### Next Steps
+            1. Review the changeset in this PR
+            2. Merge this PR to main
+            3. The automated release workflow will create a version PR
+            4. Merge the version PR to publish to npm and create a GitHub release
+
+  # GitHub reports jobs killed by timeout-minutes as cancelled rather than
+  # failed. Observe every job and excuse only cancellations that the tested
+  # workflow explicitly permits when a newer commit supersedes this run.
+  pipeline-status:
+    name: Pipeline Status
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-pipeline-status
+      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
+    if: >-
+      !cancelled()
+    needs:
+      - detect-changes
+      - test-compilation
+      - check-file-line-limits
+      - version-check
+      - changeset-check
+      - lint
+      - test
+      - docker-build
+      - docker-publish-config
+      - docker-publish-build
+      - validate-docs
+      - release-preflight
+      - release
+      - instant-release
+      - docker-publish
+      - changeset-pr
+    # actions: read lets the gate list this run's jobs and name the ones
+    # GitHub never acquired a runner for.
+    permissions:
+      actions: read
+      contents: read
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Setup Node.js
+        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
+        with:
+          node-version: '24.x'
+
+      - name: Fail the run when a required job was cancelled or failed
+        env:
+          NEEDS_JSON: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          RUN_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
+          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && format('refs/pull/{0}/head', github.event.number) || github.ref }}
+        run: bash scripts/check-pipeline-status.sh

+name: Rerun unacquired jobs
+
+# When GitHub cannot provide a hosted runner (usually macOS arm64 under
+# capacity constraints) it gives up on the job with "The job was not acquired
+# by Runner of type hosted even after multiple attempts". No code ran, yet the
+# run is red and a push to main releases nothing. This reruns such runs, at
+# most twice, and only when no job that ran steps failed.
+on:
+  # Runs the default branch's code, reads only numeric run IDs from the event,
+  # and never checks out the commit of the run it inspects.
+  workflow_run: # zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers]
+    workflows:
+      - Checks and release
+      - Example app
+      - Security
+      - Broken Link Checker
+      - Workflows
+      - JavaScript-first mixed-language example
+    types: [completed]
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+env:
+  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
+  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: init.defaultBranch
+  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main
+
+jobs:
+  rerun:
+    name: Rerun jobs that never got a runner
+    # Attempts 1 and 2 may be rerun; the script repeats these checks.
+    if: >-
+      github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'failure' &&
+      github.event.workflow_run.run_attempt < 3
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    concurrency:
+      group: rerun-unacquired-${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
+      cancel-in-progress: false
+    permissions:
+      actions: write
+      contents: read
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Setup Node.js
+        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
+        with:
+          node-version: '24.x'
+
+      - name: Rerun the run when only runner acquisition failed
+        env:
+          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+        run: node scripts/rerun-unacquired.mjs rerun

+name: Security
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+  pull_request:
+    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
+  schedule:
+    - cron: '0 6 * * 1'
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+# Least-privilege default; jobs escalate individually when needed.
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+# Provide Git config to actions/checkout itself; checkout runs git init before
+# any workflow step can configure Git.
+env:
+  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
+  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: init.defaultBranch
+  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main
+
+jobs:
+  codeql:
+    name: CodeQL (${{ matrix.language }})
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 30
+    env:
+      CODEQL_ACTION_DIFF_INFORMED_QUERIES: 'false'
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-codeql-${{ matrix.language }}
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    permissions:
+      actions: read
+      contents: read
+      security-events: write
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix:
+        language: [javascript-typescript, actions]
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Initialize CodeQL
+        uses: github/codeql-action/init@v4
+        with:
+          languages: ${{ matrix.language }}
+          config-file: ./.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml
+
+      - name: Autobuild
+        uses: github/codeql-action/autobuild@v4
+
+      - name: Analyze
+        uses: github/codeql-action/analyze@v4
+        with:
+          output: codeql-results
+
+      - name: Require clean CodeQL results
+        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
+        run: node scripts/check-codeql-results.mjs codeql-results
+
+      - name: Preserve CodeQL reports
+        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
+        uses: ./.github/actions/artifact-transport
+        with:
+          name: codeql-results-${{ matrix.language }}
+          path: codeql-results
+          if-no-files-found: error
+
+  dependency-graph:
+    name: Dependency Graph Prerequisite
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-dependency-graph
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    outputs:
+      enabled: ${{ steps.graph.outputs.enabled }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+      - name: Check dependency graph availability
+        id: graph
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
+          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before || github.sha }}
+          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
+          REQUIRE_GRAPH: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' && '1' || '0' }}
+        run: |
+          mode=()
+          if [[ "$REQUIRE_GRAPH" == 1 ]]; then mode=(--require); fi
+          bash scripts/check-dependency-graph.sh "$BASE_SHA" "$HEAD_SHA" "${mode[@]}"
+
+  dependency-review:
+    name: Dependency Review
+    needs: [dependency-graph]
+    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.dependency-graph.outputs.enabled == 'true'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-dependency-review
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+      pull-requests: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Review dependency changes
+        uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v5
+        with:
+          # Same level as the npm-audit gate; npm-audit annotates the lower
+          # severities this accepts.
+          fail-on-severity: high
+          show-openssf-scorecard: true
+          warn-on-openssf-scorecard-level: 0
+          comment-summary-in-pr: on-failure
+
+  npm-audit:
+    name: Audit npm lock (${{ matrix.directory }})
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-npm-audit-${{ matrix.directory }}
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix:
+        directory:
+          ['.', examples/universal-app, .github/actions/artifact-transport]
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
+        with:
+          node-version: 24
+
+      # Every advisory is annotated and listed in the step summary; only
+      # `high` and above fail pull requests, so a moderate advisory with no
+      # patched release cannot block every contributor. The weekly run also
+      # fails on a moderate advisory that `npm audit fix` resolves without
+      # --force, which is the signal that someone has work to do.
+      - name: Audit current lock
+        working-directory: ${{ matrix.directory }}
+        env:
+          AUDIT_DIR: ${{ matrix.directory }}
+          AUDIT_LEVEL: high
+          AUDIT_FIXABLE_LEVEL: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && 'moderate' || '' }}
+        run: node "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/scripts/npm-audit-report.mjs"
+
+  # Terminal status gate: runs even when the jobs above fail or are
+  # cancelled, and turns a `timeout-minutes` kill (reported as cancelled)
+  # into a red run. needs is derived and checked by the status-gate-coverage
+  # job in workflows.yml.
+  pipeline-status:
+    name: Pipeline Status
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-pipeline-status
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    # A status function is required: without one the gate inherits the
+    # implicit "every dependency succeeded" condition and is skipped in
+    # exactly the runs it exists to report.
+    if: >-
+      !cancelled()
+    needs:
+      - codeql
+      - dependency-review
+      - dependency-graph
+      - npm-audit
+    # actions: read lets the gate list this run's jobs and name the ones
+    # GitHub never acquired a runner for.
+    permissions:
+      actions: read
+      contents: read
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Setup Node.js
+        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
+        with:
+          node-version: '24.x'
+
+      - name: Fail the run when a required job was cancelled or failed
+        env:
+          NEEDS_JSON: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          RUN_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
+          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && format('refs/pull/{0}/head', github.event.number) || github.ref }}
+        run: bash scripts/check-pipeline-status.sh

+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches:
+      - main
+    paths:
+      - '.github/**'
+      - '**.sh'
+      - '.husky/**'
+      - 'scripts/check-ci-workflows.mjs'
+      - 'scripts/check-status-gate-covers-all-jobs.mjs'
+      - 'scripts/check-pipeline-status.sh'
+      - 'scripts/rerun-unacquired.mjs'
+      - 'scripts/github-api.mjs'
+      - 'scripts/check-artifact-archive.mjs'
+      - 'scripts/artifact-transport.mjs'
+      - 'scripts/artifact-files.mjs'
+  pull_request:
+    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
+    paths:
+      - '.github/**'
+      - '**.sh'
+      - '.husky/**'
+      - 'scripts/check-ci-workflows.mjs'
+      - 'scripts/check-status-gate-covers-all-jobs.mjs'
+      - 'scripts/check-pipeline-status.sh'
+      - 'scripts/rerun-unacquired.mjs'
+      - 'scripts/github-api.mjs'
+      - 'scripts/check-artifact-archive.mjs'
+      - 'scripts/artifact-transport.mjs'
+      - 'scripts/artifact-files.mjs'
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+# Least-privilege default; these jobs only need to read the checked-out tree.
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+# Provide Git config to actions/checkout itself; checkout runs git init before
+# any workflow step can configure Git.
+env:
+  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
+  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: init.defaultBranch
+  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main
+
+jobs:
+  actionlint:
+    name: actionlint
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-actionlint
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      # The Docker image bundles shellcheck and pyflakes, so this also lints
+      # every `run:` block. A native actionlint binary without shellcheck on
+      # PATH silently skips the shell checks and exits 0 - worth knowing when
+      # reproducing a failure locally:
+      #   docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/repo" -w /repo rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12 -color
+      # Pinned by digest because a mutable tag of a repository we do not
+      # control is arbitrary code execution in any job that holds
+      # credentials (the same reasoning as the `'*': hash-pin` policy in
+      # .github/zizmor.yml). Re-resolve when bumping:
+      #   docker pull rhysd/actionlint:<tag> &&
+      #   docker inspect --format='{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' rhysd/actionlint:<tag>
+      - uses: docker://rhysd/actionlint@sha256:b1934ee5f1c509618f2508e6eb47ee0d3520686341fec936f3b79331f9315667 # v1.7.12
+        with:
+          # queue:max is supported by GitHub; actionlint's schema lags it.
+          args: -color -ignore "unexpected key .queue. for .concurrency. section"
+
+  shellcheck:
+    name: ShellCheck
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-shellcheck
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+      - name: Check standalone shell scripts and hooks
+        run: git ls-files -z '*.sh' '.husky/*' | xargs -0 pipx run --spec shellcheck-py==0.11.0.1 shellcheck
+
+  # The terminal status job of release.yml keys branch protection; its
+  # needs list is hand-maintained, so a job left out of it could fail while
+  # the gate reports success. This derives the requirement from the
+  # workflow itself.
+  status-gate-coverage:
+    name: Status Gate Coverage
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-status-gate-coverage
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Check pinned workflow tooling and hosted runners
+        run: node scripts/check-ci-workflows.mjs
+
+      - name: Check the status gate covers every job
+        # Every workflow here runs a hand-maintained pipeline-status gate;
+        # this derives each requirement from the workflow itself.
+        run: >-
+          node scripts/check-status-gate-covers-all-jobs.mjs
+          .github/workflows/release.yml
+          .github/workflows/links.yml
+          .github/workflows/security.yml
+          .github/workflows/workflows.yml
